name: 2120 S. Prairie Avenue — the alley building of the house at 2120 (district draft; refined by T-1937)

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '2-storey brick building on the alley with a stone alley face, lettered VACANT 1ST / DRESS MAKING 2ND'. Both uses are 1911 ones. For 1904 the envelope is backcast and its use reconstructed as a stable/coach house. (Re-read: the register's "Electric Motor Repairing" is not on this building; ruling r35-2120-rear-label.)

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2351, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1937 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35 trace (s35fp-2120-b2), the T-1842 census (s35-2120-rear) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35-068; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-west-2351).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 2120 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2120 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 4.750, v -6.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation -0.685 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'service' overlaid with the frontage row: 2-storey brick, a dwelling in 1904 (the 1904 Blue Book lists the Gorton household; DRESS MAKING is the 1911 use): the brick family's low hip over two storeys and its one-storey rear wing; its frame porches stand as the sheet traces them. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 3523783087 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %.
